finished.title: Single-player stability runs
finished.body: PASS (Nov 8). Both the original and the modded game ran full 20-turn test games with mid-game saves reloading cleanly, no crashes, and no hangs. The advisor popup that blocked an earlier run is now handled on sight, and it fired five times per game without slowing anything down.

finished.title: Single-player stability runs
finished.body: BLOCKED (Nov 7). The standard build ran its full twenty turns with clean saves and reloads, but the test setup hit a voting screen it doesn't know how to dismiss yet, and stopped by its own rule. The modded build hasn't run yet. The next step is a decision on one more fix for the test setup.

finished.title: Which trade-network code really runs?
finished.body: PASS (Nov 7). Both run, at different layers: the original game code does the trade-network recompute, and the mod's replacement only takes over two pathfinding steps when its Trade Net X add-on is loaded. The performance column measures the whole recompute, not one side alone.

finished.title: Do modded save files keep their extra data?
finished.body: PASS (Nov 7). The mod's extra data rides at the very end of the save file, outside the game's own format, and is only found by reading backwards from the end. If that trailer is damaged or cut, the data silently resets to defaults. The report now lists the exact ways it can be lost, and how players can avoid them.

finished.title: Multiplayer sync: what 'in sync' actually means
finished.body: PASS (Nov 7). The game's own sync check only watches its random-number stream, and the mod's extra data never crosses the network directly, so two copies can drift apart silently. The spec now names exactly what to compare, turn by turn.

finished.title: Test lab stood up in its own virtual machine
The bug that kept ending test games early is found and fixed
finished.body: Turned out the game was fine; the tooling was misreading the year counter on screen.

finished.title: Self-continuing work sessions
finished.body: When a session fills up, it writes a checkpoint and a fresh one picks up automatically. No more lost progress.
